title: Account Policy
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Account Policy (Classic Ui)?
answer: A locked account remains locked until an administrator unlocks it or a specified amount of time passes. Locked accounts cannot log on. The also determines whether or not a remote user will be forcibly disconnected from all connections to servers in the domain if that user's logon hours expire, and whether users must log on before changing their passwords. If lockout is enabled, then a user account becomes locked if there are a number of incorrect attempts to log on to that account, occurring with no more than a specified amount of time between any two of the bad logon attempts.

question: How do I use Problems running the Agent Server (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: You cannot start the Agent Server as an application by using the Windows Remote Desktop (a terminal client). title: Audit Policy
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Audit Policy (Classic Ui)?
answer: Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer's security log. Windows can record a range of security event types, from a system-wide event such as a user logging on, to an attempt by a user to read a specific file. Both successful and unsuccessful attempts to perform an action can be recorded. When administering a Windows computer that is not a domain controller, this policy affects only the security log of that computer.

title: Available Agents
question: How do I configure Available Agents (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Steps: The AlarmManagement Agent : configures and records your active incidents so you can improve your alarming configuration. - The Alias Agent : creates a reference to an existing agent to adopt its Behaviour and state information. - The Analog Agent : stores a real (floating point) value and provides engineering functionality such as scaling. - The ARec Agent : configures up to 256 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. - The Audit agent : supplements the Agent Server auditing by monitoring one or more tags for ANY change in value.

title: Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents
question: How do I use Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database.

answer: This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: - Overloaded > 50% - Reactive 25%-50% - Stable 5%-25% - Robust 1%-5% - Predictive < 1%. answer: Steps: A VARIABLE action will alter recipe execution based on the value of the agent.slot given in the Tag/Value field, as follows: Slot value Action 0 Wait until the slot value changes to a value between 1 and 6 and then perform the action associated with this number 1 Go to next step 2 Go to previous step 3 Go to first step 4 Go to last step 5 Perform verification failure rollback 6 Stop recipe execution Note: the Tag/Value for a VARIABLE action is usually an expression or a slot that returns a Boolean value. The Tag/Value field may also be an explicit number between 0 and 6.

When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged.

title: Adroit OEM Licensing
question: What are the key specifications or limits for OEM Licensing (Smart Ui)?
answer: In Adroit certain components require a SEPARATE license BEFORE they can be used, this is known as an OEM licensed component. Note: OEM components are usually charged for although in some cases they may be free. These OEM (separately-licensed) components are no longer specified by their associated OEM codes but now included as separate textual entries in the product license, so that users can easily see exactly which components they are currently licensed for.

title: Alternate Secondary Port Enabled
question: How do I use Alternate Secondary Port Enabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources. Adroit drivers can make use of a different PLC addressing to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the PLCs used need to have separate addresses and both PLCs need to be able to be independently accessed by the Adroit drivers. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached.

title: Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit (Smart Ui)?
answer: The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means.

title: Best Practices
question: How do I configure Project Directory Structure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc. For this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created at the root drive (or wherever the data files are required to be stored), typically called ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default ', this project folder should contain the following directories: - \CSV, which should contain all your exported data. - \CustomAgents, which contains all the custom agents created for the project.

title: How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy
question: How do I use How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: - The Site level is the MAPS project. So you will have one MAPS project per site. For example, XYZ Foods. - The Area level is the defined Plant area/s of the MAPS project. For example, Batching Plant. - The Process Cell level is the PLC/s of each defined plant area. answer: This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm routes that have been configured. title: Routing to Audio Devices
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Routing to Audio Devices (Smart Ui)?
answer: Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented.

title: Secondary Port Disabled
question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Disabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: - Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. - Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured.

title: Secondary Port Enabled
question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Enabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Adroit drivers can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary port if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction.

answer: - Open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, navigate the spider workspace using the scroll bars, until you can see the required silk. - Right-click this silk and select the Silks menu. - From the Silks menu select the description of the required silk. title: SNMP Managed Objects
question: How do I configure SNMP Managed Objects (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Network devices that are managed by SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. expose their management data as managed objects. title: The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
question: How do I configure Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Note: Asynchronous or non-polling exception-based (telemetry) drivers are particularly affected by shadowed cluster servers. When a second cluster partner, is started, it will start in standby mode and then any Classic UIs configured to attach to this newly started server will display any tags that are linked to "telemetry" device(s) as being "greyed-out" or marked bad. Note: Normally, this should only be a problem on the UI of an unmanned cluster node, which is configured to connect locally, since all other remote UIs should be tracking the master.

title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Improved multi-channel performance (Smart Ui)?
answer: Previously, only specific legacy drivers supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio. All NASA drivers provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. When enabled, NASA drivers can support up to 8 channels, which are utilised as-needed to service the required transactions to achieve parallel communication on a single device.

title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
question: What are the key specifications or limits for maximum demand and why should you monitor it? (Smart Ui)?
answer: Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage.

title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Available time (Smart Ui)?
answer: Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum . - This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. - If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF.

title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Calculation duration (Smart Ui)?
answer: By default, the agent records the OEE or KPI based on shift numbers, which are determined by the Shift agent specified by the Shift tag field of the edit dialog ( shiftAgent slot). At the end of each shift the OEE or KPI is recorded and automatically reset for the start of the next shift. For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a "per batch" basis, then: - Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and - Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch.

title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
question: How do I use Complex mode and KPI calculation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode.

question: How do I use OEE calculations (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The OEE agent performs using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production.

question: How do I use Running time (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the and will raise a downtime alarm status. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot. title: TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem
question: How do I troubleshoot TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: - Backup your database (WGP file) - Unscan all the tags to that PLC. - Save and restart the Agent Server. - Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each. Steps: Check that the scan-points, within the group that have just been added have actual addresses in the PLC.

title: Diagnostic Counters Screen
question: How do I use Diagnostic Counters Screen (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The following describes all the available counters: - Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. - Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. - Retry's: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. - Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. - Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised.
